method: Resolves a request path against nginx location blocks in the documented search order. The pasted text is scanned for location headers of the form location [modifier] pattern {, accepting no modifier, =, ^~, ~ and ~*, with the opening brace on the same line or the next one, and each block records its one-based line number. Blocks are rejected rather than guessed when the list is empty, when a pattern is longer than 200 characters, when a modifier is put on a named location, when a prefix does not start with /, when a regex does not compile, or when two blocks repeat the same modifier and pattern, which nginx itself refuses as a duplicate. The match is made on the path with the query string and fragment removed. An exact = block whose pattern equals the path wins immediately. Otherwise every block without a modifier and every ^~ block whose pattern prefixes the path is collected, the longest wins, and if that longest prefix carries ^~ the search ends there. Only when it does not does the regex pass run, in file order, with ~ case-sensitive and ~* case-insensitive; the first regex that matches wins even over a longer prefix. If no regex matches the longest prefix answers, and if nothing matches the result is a 404. Every block is then labelled with its outcome: the winner, an exact block on another path, the longest prefix that was outranked, a shorter matching prefix, a prefix that does not cover the path, a regex that would have matched but lost to a ^~ prefix or an exact match, a regex that would have matched after an earlier regex, a regex that does not match, or a named @location which no URI can reach. The page also reports the match kind, the longest prefix, the block count and the reason in plain words, and warns when several regexes would match the same path so the later ones are dead for that URI. Not modelled: percent-decoding, dot-segment and repeated-slash normalisation of the URI, rewrites that change $uri before location matching, try_files and error_page fallbacks, nested locations, include and map expansion, and PCRE-only regex syntax, since patterns are compiled as JavaScript regular expressions. Pure local text processing: no storage, uploads or network access.
